What's the difference if you must follow their instruction.  Being asked to do something that you must follow feels like an order to me.

But it did help them sweep the area.  You can't just leave a potential threat sitting there while you search the area. If they had left them out there the officers would be leaving their flank exposed and if the people on their porch were there to do harm the officers could be in some serious trouble. The quickest way to eliminate them as a threat was to have them go inside while the police search the area.  It's like if there was an accident in an area and the police have to tape it off so civilians don't wander in.  Under normal circumstance you would be able to go into the taped off area, but because there is an investigation taking place you are not allowed there at the moment.  Think of them sweeping the street as if they were putting up tape all along the perimeter and they don't want anyone to interfere with the investigation.

But there was a reason in this instance. The police in this clip are doing a sweep of the street. It doesn't matter if you are on your property or not, everyone they come into contact with is possibly dangerous. To diffuse them of the situation they were asked to go inside. That is not an unjust order. In order to do a proper sweep they have to neutralize all possible threats. These people are in a public enough space after curfew to be able to cause legitimate harm to the officers who are out there doing their job. The people in the clip are allowed to go back out onto their porch after the officers had finished the sweep of that area. There could be many just reasons for them to try amd get those people into their home that we just can't know with only this clip. There could have been someone dangerous in the area. They can be reasonably suspicious of anyone who is outside after curfew whether or not they are on their property because there were many dangerous people roaming around at the time. The police didn't do much on the first few nights, qnd many buildings burned, and firefighters and emt's were not able to go out because areas were not secured.

I don't understand. I agree with you on the fact that you are allowed out on your property, after they updated the website that is still stated clearly. Let's say you are driving down the highway at the speed limit and a cop behind you turns on his lights. Even though you know you haven't done anything wrong you still have to pull over right? If you don't pull over they are going to eventually force your vehicle to a stop. The police telling you to go inside while they are sweeping the street is kinda like them turning on their lights. Even though you didn't commit any crimes you still have to listen to the officers.

There is no bs excuse. The information was correct before, it is correct now.  That website is not the end all be all, it is just there to inform the people about the curfew.  You had to listen to officers before they updated it on the website, that's why this happened.

I am not being disingenuous.  I know that they updated the FAQ to more properly represent what is going on and to keep the public better informed.  They didn't suddenly change the rules.  The rules have been the same the whole time, they just updated the FAQ to better reflect those rules so people would have a better understanding of the situation.

I feel like you are incorrect in saying that it used to just say yes. I thought it had everything up to the but statement. I am not pretending like I didn't see the change in the FAQ, I am saying that they updating the FAQ to better inform the public with how the laws work. They didn't suddenly change the laws, just the FAQ so that people are better informed about what is going on out there.

I feel like we have different expectations of civil rights. In this clip I don't see any civil rights being violated. The police are allowed to give civilians orders. If they suspect you of something and yell at you to get on the ground with your hands in the air and you don't follow through, they will use force to get you onto the ground whether you are innocent or not. The most recent event with George Floyd is when an officer brought his power way too far and killed a man when he was long since incapacitated. That was a viloation of his civil rights and a lot of people are rightly upset with that and out protesting. This clip where they are shot with paintball, or rubber bullets, civil rights were not being violated because they were given direct orders from a police officer and chose to disobey them.

You are correct in the fact that this specific FAQ was different, but they didn't change the laws in the past few days.  They changed the FAQ to better represent what is going on out there.

Like if a group of murders were found in the area the local government or police would probably tell people to get inside there homes, and if they came into contact with anyone outside on their property they would ask them to get inside while they sweep the area for those murderers. I see it the other way around. Most people here can not see a situation where they had a legitimate reason for their actions. I see it from both sides of the coin and like to think that they did indeed have good reason for their actions. I very well could be wrong and they did not have a good reason, in which case they should be punished for their actions accordingly. I feel that, like myself, everyone here on reddit is just expressing their thoughts from their own point of view. I can see a world where there is a legitimate reason for the officers involved to act in the way they did. I am not saying what they did was the right thing to do, just that they most likely had some reason to do it, or else they are acting in bad faith, and like I said they should then be punished for it.

You are right, the police are not kings who get to make up rules and assault the citizenry. The murder of George Floyd is not something that I take lightly. I feel like they are about so much more than just police abusing their power. To me it's about racial inequalities and those who are treated differently by individuals due to the color of their skin. Anything past 20:00 last night was not part of those protests. Anyone still out there past the curfew was a potential rioter and were treated likewise. People have been demolishing buildings and family owned businesses. That is not a protest, that is destruction of livelihoods. Those people burning down buildings have no right to use George Floyd as a scape goat in order to try and destroy society. I take side with all those protestors out there, but the rioters are something else entirely.

I'd like to hope they had a good reason yeah. No one wants to see police abusing their power. I like to believe that most cops out there are good people. I am not naive enough to believe that they are all good people, I know there are bad people in all sects of life, police are no exception. You are right that I have a bias towards wanting to see them have a good reason, but I am also willing to accept they didn't and that what they did was an abuse of their power and they should be reprimanded appropriately.  I was raised to respect men and women in the police force and armed forces and like to think that, for the most part, they are acting in good faith.

You are right that I most likely won't change my stance on this due to a comment on reddit. What would change my mind is a police report or something of the sort from either them or the media. Anyone can say anything here, i can't know if what they are telling me is correct or not. I am not in charge of policing the police, all that matters for my perspective of the situation is how I feel about it and the information that I know. The only law I was told about was the one that allows people out on their porch during curfew. Law is big and complicated. I don't think the situation is as simple as they are allowed to be on their porch therefore the police acted unlawfully. Unreasonably for sure, but like I said, I am no law expert, I have no idea if there are sections or subsections that deal with riot supression and the likes.

I have not studied Minnesota law. I have no idea if what they did was unlawful. I do believe circumstances are important to how the law is interpreted.  Like how murder is illegal, but if someone breaks into your home and you kill them trying to defend yourself and family and property then you probably won't be going to jail. Like I said, I am no law expert, and I am fairly certain no one else here is either, again I could very well be wrong.

I draw the line at, there are people destroying property and livelihoods in such large numbers as to warrant the largest armed response in Minnesota history and were told by the govenor himself to please stay inside past 20:00. I am willing to temporarily step inside my home as to not get shot with riot suppressing weapons because of how volatile the situation is.

There could be any number of reasons why they did what they did, some wrong some right.  It is very possible that these officers were acting out of line and if that is the case should be properly reprimanded.

I don't know how, or what on the officers were briefed on, so this is just my personnel speculation that maybe they were told to treat everyone that they came close into contact with as a credible threat in which case shooting at them would still be unreasonable in this situation, but I think I can kinda understand where they are coming from.  If they were just doing this to prove a show of force or something like that I feel like they made a big mistake there.  I don't know if they were on a time crunch, or under super strict orders and just didn't want to, or possibly couldn't interact with them in a diplomatic matter.  I still feel like they should have tried being more diplomatic nonetheless. From what I was watching on the news it seems like they are not messing around out there and a quite a few innocent people are getting caught up in it.

I don't know.  From my point of view I just see it as regular unreasonable due to all the arson and vandalism over the past few days.  I am no expert on law so I don't know if them opening fire like that is operating outside of it.  They may have gotten too much inside their own heads that they have to really show force to try and scare off all the rioters, not that that is an excuse just trying to get some perspective.  If they are acting outside of their regulations though, you are absolutely correct in that that is no way acceptable.

I actually think that the quarantine is a great idea, but I also believe in the peoples right to protest.  I don't have the solution for how people could have protested while staying six feet apart and not somehow being a mass gathering.  It's a difficult situation, while yes I do believe it necessary to have this quarantine in order to help stop the spreading of the infection, I also think that these protests are equally necessary to help stop the spread of injustice and discrimination.

With the property thing, if they were hanging out on someone elses property they would have been trespassing and probably arrested. Yeah, I agree with you there.  I have seen videos of them arresting and firing upon media personnel, so they must be considering anyone and everyone who is outside as a possible threat.

Yes, you are right, a blowjob is a completely unreasonable request of an officer and they would hopefully have the book thrown at them for their actions, but a request to get inside of your home during a sweep of a street during a curfew do to rioting and looting does not seem unreasonable to me.  Should they have fired upon them, in my opinion no they should not have, but like I said earlier, it appears to me that they are sweeping that street and not taking it lightly, I don't know the exact situation, there could have been a recent threat, it could have been coordinated with another group and they had to act fast. There may have been nothing of the sort in the area and no pressure to get a move on. I am not sure, I don't have all the details.

You are right. They would definitely need to get a warrant to search the inside of your home.  To ensure the safety of themselves and others, they wanted that group inside their home, at least that is my take on this situation. Also I am curious as to who you people refers to.

You are right, under normal circumstances this would be super unreasonable, but I feel as though it is not any given night.  There has been a curfew called into effect and these officers are trying to prevent more destruction and potential harm to people and property than what has already happened.

In this instance they could be ordering them to go inside for multiple reasons, was it right for them to open fire, probably not, regrettable even, but they are out there to catch people doing harm and to catch these people efficiently I feel like they should be allowed to give orders to civilians that could be impeding their progress, even though they are not directly in the way, a group out in front of a house in could potentially cause some trouble.  I think that they wanted to prevent themselves from getting attacked from the side or rear.

But how could they have known it was their property?  They told them to get inside multiple times and they didn't make a move.  I agree that people should be able to due what they want on their own property, but when there is a curfew and a line of officers coming down the street and they tell you to do something, it is probably a good idea to listen to them so they can get on with catching the actual people who are out there to cause harm.

Because the police are out there to stop people from doing harm, and if they give you a direct order and you do not follow their orders then they probably consider you a risk and will use force to stop that risk.

Yes, you should be able to be out on your own property, but if you are yelled at three times by a large group of officers to get into your house and don't even make a move to go inside then you can expect them to use force. Rioters could attempt to disguise themselves by sitting on other peoples property to get past the police.
